summary: Dedicated pool throughput drop with intermittent GPU allocation failures; autoscaler not recovering
description:
Issue summary: Over the past 3 hours VeloxHealth is seeing a sustained drop in throughput from their dedicated GPU pool in us-west-2. Average token/sec for pinned model gpt-large-16k-4bit dropped ~55% and tail latency increased. The autoscaler did not provision additional nodes despite queue depth increasing and there are intermittent GPU allocation failures reported by the scheduler (alloc error:  'no healthy GPU available' for short bursts).

Impact: Production traffic for VeloxHealth (critical account) experienced degraded throughput causing request timeouts and some fallbacks to smaller models. This affects multiple endpoints and has visible customer-facing errors (5xx and timeouts).

Environment: prod/us-west-2, Dedicated pool: velox-prod-pool-3, autoscaler policy: cpu+queue heuristics (scale-up threshold: queue>8 for 60s), instance type: p4d-like, runtime version: serving-runtime v1.9.2, scheduler v2.3.

Timeline: 2026-03-13 09:10 UTC - first customer alert. 09:15 UTC - SRE triaged; observed queue growth. 09:40 UTC - manual mitigation (migrate high-priority routes to fallback pool) began. 11:12 UTC - intermittent GPU allocation failures logged. 12:00 UTC - mitigation: increased pool headroom by 20% via manual resize; throughput partially recovered.

Logs & signals:
- Scheduler logs show repeated "alloc failed: no healthy GPU available" spikes between 10:50-11:30 UTC.
- Autoscaler metrics show scale-up events triggered but not reflected in cluster size; scaling API returned 202 but node provisioning timeouts seen in cloud provider logs.
- Node-level metrics show elevated GPU utilization on 2 hosts (95% sustained) with adjacent hosts idle — suggests noisy-neighbor contention on PCIe or host-level I/O.
- Traces show KV cache misses increased after 09:20 UTC which amplified token generation cost per request.

Immediate ask: Investigate autoscaler failures to provision nodes and scheduler allocation errors; determine whether noisy neighbor or host-level resource starvation is causing allocation failures. Provide mitigation steps and a timeline for full recovery.
steps_to_reproduce: Send steady production-like traffic pattern to velox-prod-pool-3 targeting gpt-large-16k-4bit at current QPS used by customer (~120 rps).
Observe queue depth and autoscaler metrics for 20 minutes while adding short bursts (30s) of 2x traffic every 5 minutes.
Watch scheduler logs for 'alloc failed' messages and check cloud provider node provisioning events / quota errors.
Check per-host GPU utilization and host-level errs (NVML GPU ECC errors, PCIe resets, cloud instance health checks).
investigation_notes: 2026-03-13 10:05 UTC - SRE (Ezra): initial hypothesis: autoscaler ignored scale-up signals due to transient cloud API 429s. Checking cloud provider quotas and recent rate-limits.

2026-03-13 10:48 UTC - Eng (Marta): scheduler logs show allocation failures with reason 'insufficient device memory' on a subset of hosts while other hosts report <30% memory usage. Possible driver/visibility bug or noisy-tenant causing misreporting.
2026-03-13 11:20 UTC - Observed host-level PCIe errors on host i-0a1b2c3d; NVML reports GPU reset events. Marked host as suspect and fenced it from scheduling (manual).

2026-03-13 11:45 UTC - Manual pool resize applied (+3 instances). Cloud provider reports 2 provisioning timeouts due to AZ-level capacity in us-west-2a; autoscaler retries suppressed by backoff logic (current backoff 12m).
2026-03-13 12:05 UTC - After fencing suspect hosts and adding headroom, throughput recovered to ~80% of baseline. No further 'alloc failed' errors for 30 minutes.

2026-03-13 10:10 - Ezra Coleman (SRE): Investigating autoscaler and scheduler logs. Opening cloud support case if provider quota issues found.
2026-03-13 11:00 - Marta Ruiz (Eng): Possible noisy-neighbor on host i-0a1b2c3d; NVML resets seen. Suggest fencing host and validating HW health.
2026-03-13 11:40 - Ezra Coleman (SRE): Applied manual fencing and triggered a manual resize for pool velox-prod-pool-3 (+3). Will monitor.

2026-03-13 12:20 - Priya Kapoor (Support): Notified customer of temporary mitigation and asked to validate impact on their traffic. Customer reports lower error rate but some increased latency on older pinned routes.
2026-03-14 08:15 - Leah Park (Account): Customer requests RCA and whether we will offer credit for the incident. Adding Finance if needed.
resolution_notes: Workarounds applied: fenced two suspect hosts and manually increased pool headroom (+3 instances) which reduced allocation failures and restored throughput to ~80% baseline. Next steps: (1) follow up with cloud provider on AZ capacity events and node provisioning timeouts; (2) run hardware diagnostics on fenced hosts and replace if faults confirmed; (3) adjust autoscaler backoff logic to be more tolerant to transient provisioning errors; (4) add a circuit that routes high-priority customers to reserved spare capacity to prevent customer-impacting fallbacks. Owner: Ezra Coleman. Target: full recovery + RCA by 2026-03-16.
follow_up_tasks: Open cloud support ticket for provisioning timeouts and AZ capacity report (owner: Ezra).
Run stress and NVML diagnostics on fenced hosts; escalate to hardware replacement if errors reproducible (owner: Marta).
Propose autoscaler change: reduce exponential backoff ceiling for provisioning retries and add compensating manual override route (owner: infra-team).
Create postmortem and customer-facing RCA; coordinate with Account for credits if warranted (owner: Priya).
